title: Preflight orchestration: unify smoke, perf, and eval signals into a single pass/fail gate
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current preflight checks are an array of independent pass/fail jobs (smoke, perf regression, eval-suites, rollout-sanity) run in parallel. Each produces its own verdict and human reviewers manually reconcile conflicting signals for canaries and LTS channel upgrades. This causes slow merges, opaque failures, and occasional blocked rollouts despite benign regressions.

Goal: Implement a preflight orchestration layer that ingests multiple signals, applies configurable weightings and hard-fail criteria, and emits a single deterministic gate decision (pass/warn/fail) plus a compact rationale. The system must support per-release and per-channel policies (e.g., strict LTS thresholds vs. permissive nightly), be audit-log friendly, and be callable from CI, the Console rollout pipeline, and the Dedicated upgrade runner.

Scope:
- Design signal schema for smoke, performance summary, eval-suite regressions, and telemetry-based canary deltas.
- Implement the lightweight orchestration service (stateless decision module + persistent event log).
- Provide default policy profiles: nightly, stable, LTS-strict.
- Integrate with existing preflight jobs and dashboards; add a single JSON verdict artifact to CI and a human-readable summary to Console.
- Add an automatic mitigation suggestion engine: fallback model variant, decreased batch size, or roll back dependent rollout policy.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term ML-driven anomaly scoring, UI redesign of Console (we will add a short summary link), and audit storage beyond current retention windows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestration service produces a single JSON verdict artifact for a preflight run that includes: overall_status (pass/warn/fail), contributing_signals with scores, primary_reason, and recommended_action.
2) Default policy profiles exist (nightly, stable, LTS-strict) and are applied based on release channel passed to the orchestrator.
3) CI pipeline consumes verdict artifact and blocks merge on 'fail' for LTS-strict and stable channels; nightly may allow 'warn' without blocking.
4) Visibility: Console shows the verdict summary link and dashboard displays aggregated preflight failure reasons over last 30 days.
5) Demo run: produce a synthetic canary with an intentional perf regression and show that the orchestrator emits 'warn' under nightly and 'fail' under LTS-strict with recommended_action set to 'pause rollout' and 'pin previous model version'.
implementation_notes:
Decision model: combine signals via weighted scoring plus hard-fail rules. Each signal must include: id, type, timestamp, baseline_metric, observed_metric, delta_percent, confidence, and artifacts (link to logs/PR).

Weights (initial): smoke=0.5, perf=0.3, eval=0.15, telemetry=0.05. Hard-fail rules: any smoke test critical assertion failure => fail immediately; perf regression > 15% at p95 for latency on dedicated workloads => fail for LTS-strict; eval-suite catastrophic quality drop (>=5% accuracy delta on critical prompts) => fail.

Storage: verdict artifacts are stored in CI artifact store (15 days) and a compressed index entry is appended to preflight-event-log in existing datastore. No new long-term DB for this sprint.

APIs: POST /preflight/run -> returns run_id; GET /preflight/run/{id}/verdict -> JSON artifact. Webhook: orchestrator emits webhook to Console and CI on final verdict.

Backward compatibility: Orchestrator will accept current job output formats; adapters will be added for legacy perf job schema.

Testing: end-to-end synthetic workflow uses the synthetic-workload-fabric (ENG-62321) with three model variants and reproducible RNG seed so decisions are deterministic for CI flakes triage.
runbook_summary:
Runbook highlights:
- Trigger a manual re-eval by re-posting the run with query param ?force=true (used for tools/infra fixes).
- If orchestrator service returns 500, fall back to presenting raw job outputs and mark gate as 'degraded'.
- On persistent false positives for perf: increase sampling or rebaseline using controlled perf harness.
- For LTS upgrades that fail the gate, use 'rollback-and-stabilize' flow: pause all rollouts, pin previous runtime image, and schedule hotfix window.
- Emergency bypass: security-approved bypass token can force release; bypasses are logged and audited.
metrics_and_dashboards:
New dashboard panels: preflight-run-rate, preflight-pass-rate-by-channel, top-5 failure reasons, mean-time-to-fix (by failure reason), and per-model per-channel regression deltas. Alerting: on >5% increase in fail-rate over baseline within 24h a ticket is auto-created and paging goes to the release team.

Metric thresholds: target pass-rate for stable >= 98%, for LTS >= 99.5%. Investigate if pass-rate drops below target for two consecutive days.

Dashboards will be linked under Console -> Rollouts -> Preflight Health.
test_matrix:
Signal types and example checks: 
- Smoke: basic end-to-end request/response sanity, KV cache warm-up, basic function-calling paths. Failure mode: schema mismatch or 500s.
- Perf: p50/p95 latency, token throughput and GPU utilization under standard synthetic batch. Failure mode: increase >15% (LTS) or >25% (nightly) in p95.
- Eval-suite: curated prompt set across safety/quality domains. Failure mode: accuracy drop >=5% on critical prompts or degradation in toxicity/safety signals.
- Telemetry: canary traffic delta for error-rate and hallucination-rate proxies. Failure mode: error-rate spike >3x baseline.

Matrix includes required artifacts links (logs, flamegraphs, KV cache hit rates) for each signal so human reviewer can triage quickly.
rollout_interaction:
Integration points:
- CI: PR checks will call orchestrator and require 'pass' for stable/LTS merges.
- Console: rollout pipeline will consult orchestrator verdict before progressing canary stages; on 'warn' the pipeline will pause and surface recommended_action.
- Dedicated upgrade runner: orchestrator verdict will be consulted by autopilot; autopilot will follow recommended_action if configured (default: pause + alert).

Channel semantics: nightly -> permissive, stable -> blocking on 'fail', LTS-strict -> blocking on 'warn' or 'fail' depending on policy. Policies are configurable via YAML in repo: .preflight/policies/{channel}.yaml.
decisions: Use weighted scoring plus hard-fail rules to keep deterministic behaviour and allow easy tuning
Store only compressed verdict index entries in long-term datastore; keep artifacts in CI for 15 days to limit cost
Initial weights favor smoke and perf to reflect production reliability priorities
Expose simple webhook and artifact API rather than adding deep Console integration in this sprint
